threads.title: The 'start' of the serve
threads.body: To me its when the person starts to release the ball in the air (or start to drop it if an underarm serve). Note the ball can still be in the person's hand but its the act of starting to release the ball is what counts. People do many different things before serving eg. Becker's rocking motion. Most will bounce the ball at the very start. But is it a general consensus that the start of the serve is when the server starts releasing the ball in the air?

threads.title: Lock out tension vs constant pull with different strings
threads.body: Hi, I've recently bought a Gamma Momentum ST and I've been stringing my rackets with poly strings at 52 lbs on this machine. On the RacquetTune App, I'm getting a reading of about 44 lbs. This is the same reading I got when the shop would string with a constant pull at 48 lbs. So in my mind, 48 lbs on a constant pull = 52 lbs on a lock-out machine (8% increase). threads.title: Who Cares about Recoil Weight?
threads.body: Advanced players care about recoil, and here’s why. Swingweight, twist weight, and recoil weight (also called ‘hitting weight’) all measure the inertia of a racquet along different axes or planes. Recoil weight shares the same plane as swingweight but its axis is the balance point (vs. the hand), and that makes it a piece of the racquet puzzle you never knew you were missing. RW measures how close a frame’s weighting is to its poles. The higher the recoil, the more polarized it is... Read more
